newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy calls in French envoy after Chirac speech.
newsitem.headline: Italy calls in French envoy after Chirac speech.

text.p: Italy on Tuesday said it had summoned France's ambassador, Jean-Bernard Merimee, to the prime minister's office.

A brief official statement said Merimee had been received but did not elaborate. It was issued after French President Jacques Chirac cast doubt in a speech in northern France on Italy's ability to join a planned European single currency.
"The Ambassador of France in Rome, Jean-Bernard Merimee, was summoned to Palazzo Chigi (the prime minister's office) and received this afternoon," the Italian statement said.

Chirac, who is scheduled to meet Prime Minister Romano Prodi for a bilateral summit later this week, said earlier he was not sure Italy would meet the economic criteria needed to join the single currency from its planned start in January 1999.
"It may take a little bit longer for those who are further behind, like Italy," Chirac said.
His remarks drew an angry response from the Italian government. Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni called for the remarks to be withdrawn and said Chirac should not interfere in Italy's affairs.
